heading: Background
excerpt: The devices in IIoT are mostly battery operated and hence cannot afford to keep their radio on for long hours. Hence the transmission, reception and sleep routines of nodes has to be scheduled to save their energy and to provide a synchronized connection in the network. The nodes in TSCH network communicate using a scheduling matrix composed of cells which are designated by its time slot index and the channel index. Recently, learning algorithms such as machine learning (ML) and reinforcement learning (RL) methods are being adopted to address resource allocation problems in wireless networks [2]. Cobbe et al. proposed the PPG, by modifying the traditional actor-critic policy gradient method [3]. In PPG, the policy and the value functions are learnt independently so that the sharing of network parameters between the value optimization and the policy optimization networks can be regulated.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: During policy phase, the agent is trained using proximal policy optimization (PPO) [5]. During auxiliary phase, the features from the value function are distilled into the policy network, so that the future policy phases improve.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: In auxiliary phase, the joint objective function that includes behavioral cloning loss and an arbitrary auxiliary loss is used to optimized the policy network.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: We consider that the network consists of 70 nodes communicating to a border router over a maximum of 3 hops. We compare the performance of our proposed scheduling algorithm with that of PPO [5] based algorithm and the Minimum Scheduling Function (MSF) [6], which is a default scheduling algorithm in TSCH networks.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: It can be seen that the PPG achieves a better reward than PPO right from the starting of the training phase and converges quickly.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: We show that the PPG improves the system throughput by 58% compared to the default scheduling algorithm MSF and 22% over the proximal policy optimization method (PPO).

heading: Background
excerpt: In 5G, the most popular approach to accomodate low latency users in the same network is through puncturing. The high data rate eMBB users are punctured and a minislot worth of resource is used by URLLC user.

heading: Background
excerpt: The punctured EMBB users experience a degradation in reliability [14]. As more resource blocks are punctured, the error probability in decoding the block becomes difficult.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: To circumvent this, we introduce a hybrid scheme that switches to orthogonal multiplexing mode for a fixed number of RBs and puncturing mode for the rest of the RBs whenever the URLLC arrival rate shoots up.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: Let K be the number of RBs dedicated to URLLC data and N be the total number of resource blocks in a minislot.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: The results highlight that the baseline puncturing strategy experiences performance degradation much earlier under increasing traffic load. In contrast, the DQN agent maintains superior performance by dynamically adapting its actions at each time slot, effectively addressing the reliability demands of both URLLC and eMBB services. However, even the DQN approach reaches a saturation point at very high arrival rates, constrained by the system’s total available bandwidth and throughput.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: The DQN-based approach consistently outperforms the baseline, keeping latency significantly lower across all λu. While the baseline exhibits a sharp increase in delay—exceeding 8 ms under high traffic—the DQN model effectively mitigates queue build-up through dynamic resource adaptation.

heading: Background
excerpt: The primary features are insufficient to predict the network attacks with very high precision. Derived features are generated by applying some statistical functions or transformations to the primary features. These derived features give us greater insight into the behavior of the network in case of an attack. ASNM dataset provides a large set of derived features. Generating a large number of derived features increases the complexity of the model. Hence feature selection techniques become important.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: We apply Chi-squared Test feature selection technique on the Advanced Security Network Metrics dataset to choose highly dependent features and remove features independent of the classifier output.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: We build a Logistic Regression based and a Neural Network based IDS on this dataset and obtain a highly accurate Network attack detection model.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: We perform a 5-fold cross validation on all the three datasets, where each dataset is split into 5 stratified sets and the mean of the individual performance metrics are recorded.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: After use of Chi-squared test, we obtain a good performance result and the classifier trains much faster. The number of nodes in the input layer reduces, so the number of computations also reduces greatly.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: Flow based features and their derived features give us better performance over the primary features, but the flow based features have a larger memory footprint. Feature Selection methods in combination with Deep Learning algorithms is one of the best solutions to intrusion detection systems. We can compromise on number of features in case of timing constraints.

heading: Background
excerpt: Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) plays a pivotal role in modern wireless communication systems, enabling receivers to autonomously identify modulation schemes without requiring prior knowledge of the transmitter’s settings. This capability is essential for enhancing the efficiency, robustness, and adaptability of real-time applications such as 5G networks, dynamic spectrum allocation, and interference mitigation.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: The Hybrid 1 model integrates the strengths of the RanNet and VGG architectures to create a novel hybrid approach. The core idea is to enhance the feature extraction capabilities of RanNet by incorporating additional layers from VGG. Specifically, a convolutional layer with a maxpooling layer and a skip connection is added between the two Ranblocks, aimed at retaining critical information during initial processing.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: Inspired by the Chain Residual Pooling block from RefineNet, the X block improves the model’s ability to capture contextual information from large input regions.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: In this architecture, two Ranblocks are employed, each incorporating an X block in place of the traditional Feablock.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: At an SNR of 18 dB, the Hybrid 2 model achieves an accuracy of 87.69%, as shown in Fig. 10.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: The comparison shows that Hybrid 1 and Hybrid 2 models achieve higher classification accuracies at most SNR levels, with Hybrid 1 slightly outperforming Hybrid 2 at very low SNR values. Hybrid 3, while still competitive, demonstrates lower accuracy, indicating that the architectural enhancements in Hybrid 1 and Hybrid 2 are more effective in improving classification performance.

heading: Background
excerpt: However, whether an ML-based NIDS can successfully handle a new type of attack is an open question. CNN-based IDS can classify these types of attacks to a certain extent but they classify most unknown attacks as benign. Due to this problem, a robust outlier detection in the NIDS system becomes necessary. The purpose of this paper is to address this vital issue.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: We put forward a Robust NIDS model, called RNIDS, which is a combination of CNN followed by an outlier detection system. The combined system classifies known attacks and identifies new outliers with high accuracy.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: We further analyze the prediction probabilities of the neural network using nearest neighbor approximation. This information helps us decide if a new adversary was attempting a malicious attack on the network.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: If the average distance is beyond a certain threshold dth, then the point is classified as a new adversary.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: The CNN model with 13 attack classes has classified different attacks with an overall accuracy of 98.3%.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: Compared to the results in Table V, Botnet, Port scan and SSH Patator are predicted as a new adversary with an accuracy of 74.96%, 88.03% and 90.08%.

heading: Major outcomes

heading: Background
excerpt: IEEE 802.15.4e standard does not define the algorithm for computing the scheduling matrix and is open to implementation. Hence the problem of designing efficient schedule in TSCH networks has gained importance in networking research community.

heading: Proposed scheme
excerpt: In initiation stage, a set of random schedules are generated. To improve the existing set of scheduling algorithms, we employ the migration and mutation operations. Migration operation shares the good features from best scheduling algorithm to the poor ones by appropriately modelling the immigration and emigration of each node in the network. Mutation operation maintains the diversity in the candidate schedules to tackle the sporadic changes in the network.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: It has been shown through simulations that the proposed BIOS scheduling algorithm achieves an improvement of 60% in delay performance and upto 40% of energy efficiency compared to MSF.

heading: Major outcomes
excerpt: In the mobile TSCH networks, the topology changes frequently forcing BIOS to explore more solutions by mutation operation which makes the solution convergence slower.

heading: Background
excerpt: In TSCH, the time is divided into slots and the bandwidth is divided into orthogonal channels [4]. The nodes in TSCH network communicate in a scheduling matrix composed of cells. The cells are the basic resource units for communication in TSCH network which are designated by its time slot index and the channel index.
